answer: One defense is a time-locked bond: a new agent must lock collateral that thaws like a glacier, only a sliver per epoch, so its reputation reaches zenith only after months of consistent work. Peers bridge trust to a newcomer only once that lock has aged. An attacker wanting a thousand identities must post a thousand bonds and freeze that capital for the whole ramp, and collusion caught before the unlock slashes every linked bond at once.
